notes: Expected shapes are the RAW parse (pre-resolveParsed), so DateRefs stay symbolic.
expect.unparsed is a boolean: we assert wording was DEFERRED, not that it was echoed verbatim.
Tier 5 rows are mostly-unexpressible on purpose. The right answer there is to defer, and the failure mode being measured is a model that invents a rule instead.

cases.text: no player plays more than 2 matches a day
cases.trap: RE-BASELINED 2026-08-17 (3rd re-baseline of this corpus): was defer-all, because rule 8 forbade compiling a per-player cap at all. every_person now exists and carries NO id, so the id-invention objection that keeps entrant/person/pool out of the parser's Scope does not apply. Emitting competition scope here is STILL the bug - it caps a 60-player event at two matches a day.

cases.text: each team plays twice a day at most
cases.trap: RE-BASELINED 2026-08-17, same wave as t01. per-TEAM, so every_entrant and NOT every_person: a team is an entry, not a human. Choosing every_person here would be wrong in the direction that matters - it would bind each player rather than each side.

cases.text: put the semifinals on Friday
cases.trap: Selector has terminal and ext_key only - no stage or round addressing

cases.text: make sure Alice doesn't play twice in a row
cases.trap: person scope does not exist in Scope

cases.text: run division Open Singles between the 5th and the 9th of September 2026
cases.trap: schema PERMITS a division-scoped window; resolveParsed rejects it later. The raw layer must emit it faithfully, not pre-censor.

cases.text: keep mornings relaxed
cases.trap: a preference: belongs in soft, and soft is NOT unparsed

cases.text: no two matches on the same court back to back
cases.trap: court/venue is not in the constraint vocabulary

cases.text: avoid clashing with the football final on TV
cases.trap: external event, nothing to compile against

cases.trap: ordering relative to other fixtures is not expressible

cases.text: Let's schedule a match and run for 4 days and keep 2 matches in the morning and 3 matches in the afternoon also we have lunch break from 12PM to 1PM
cases.trap: OWNER EXAMPLE. RE-BASELINED TWICE on 2026-08-16 as its gaps closed: the run-length gap (span end) and the mid-day break gap (no_play_between). The lunch break is now REQUIRED, not deferred. Still KNOWN-AMBIGUOUS on one clause: the sentence states no start day, so a model that also compiles {window start:today|tomorrow, end:span 4} is arguably right and will be scored as having invented it. Do not read a c01 failure as an invention without checking which clause caused it. Only the morning/afternoon split is genuinely unexpressible - max_fixtures_per_day counts a WHOLE day, so compiling it as 5 states a rule the organiser never gave.

cases.text: we play over the weekend, 6 matches on Saturday and 4 on Sunday, finals Sunday evening
cases.trap: per-DATE caps are not expressible (the cap is scope-wide); only the terminal-on-Sunday half compiles

cases.text: start 9am, finish by 9pm, 90 minutes between a player's own matches, max 8 a day, from tomorrow to next Friday
cases.trap: five legitimate rules at once - the long-but-fully-expressible case

cases.text: Open Singles: 2 a day, no earlier than 10; Mixed Doubles: 3 a day, no later than 7pm
cases.trap: four rules across two division scopes, semicolon-separated

cases.text: lunch break from 12 to 1
cases.trap: RE-BASELINED 2026-08-16. Was expect:{hard:[],unparsed:true} because the parser had no word for a mid-day break - though the ENGINE has modelled Blackout all along. no_play_between now exists, so the correct answer changed. not_after 12:00 still silently deletes the afternoon and now scores as an invention.

cases.text: run for 4 days from Monday
cases.trap: RE-BASELINED 2026-08-16. Was expect:{hard:[],unparsed:true} because a run length had no representation - and the bench caught the model filling that gap twice, first with a fabricated 2024 date and then with an invented THU. The span end now exists, so the correct answer changed: state the length, let resolveParsed count. A model that still computes the end weekday itself now fails on `invented`.

cases.text: at least 45 minutes between a player's own matches and 30 minutes before the round they feed into
cases.trap: both rest_scopes stated separately - must NOT collapse to a single 'both'

cases.text: everything after 2pm except the final which can be earlier
cases.trap: exception semantics are not expressible; the base bound compiles, the exception must defer

cases.text: no player plays twice in a row
cases.trap: REPLACES t01/t02 in the deferral cohort after their 2026-08-17 re-baseline. Still a per-entity concept and still out of vocabulary: consecutiveness is a POSITION IN THE ORDER, and min_rest_minutes is a clock. Added so the deferral cohort does not shrink to the point where the invented-rule metric stops biting.

cases.text: we can only run 8 matches a day across the whole event
cases.trap: THE RULE-8 GUARD, kept as a corpus row now that the prompt sentence protecting it is gone. This really is a whole-run cap, so competition scope is correct and every_person would be wrong. Pairs with t01/t02, which move the other way: inverting rule 8 must not drag every day cap onto a universal scope.

cases.text: run at most 10 matches a day and no player plays more than 2
cases.trap: BOTH caps in one sentence, and they do NOT conflict - a whole-run cap and a per-player cap are different rules at different scopes. Guards the scopeKey fix: while every non-division scope collapsed to the literal 'competition', conflictKeyOf gave these two the same identity and refuseContradictions dropped one.
